conventions.convention: V is a separable reflexive real Banach space, H is a real Hilbert space, and i:V→H is injective, continuous and dense. The canonical map is Jh(v)=(h,iv)H; all pairings are real and bilinear. Weak time derivatives initially assign no endpoint values.

The concrete pivot branch uses bounded open Ω⊆R^d, d≥1, 1<p<∞ and p>max(1,2d/(d+2)); W0^{1,p} is the closure of compactly supported smooth functions. Compact embedding into L2 requires no boundary regularity and assumes AC.

Flux continuity, growth, coercivity and monotonicity hold outside one common spatial null set for every pair of gradient arguments. The flux is independent of time, V carries the gradient norm, and p'=p/(p−1).
Conformity alone is insufficient: H-orthogonal projectors must be uniformly bounded V→V and converge strongly to the identity on V. Time partitions have vanishing maximum step.

The concrete mesh branch has fixed polynomial degree, global quasi-uniformity and shape regularity. In d≥2 it uses matching affine simplices; d=1 uses separately defined interval partitions. Boundary nodal coefficients vanish, and an empty interior-node space is the zero space.
The quasi-interpolant construction additionally requires Lipschitz boundary graph charts in d≥2, or finitely many intervals with disjoint closures in d=1.

Discrete states use the right-endpoint value on (t_{n−1},t_n]; D is the backward difference quotient. Compactness uses 1<p<∞ and 1<q≤∞, with an additional uniform H bound for convergence in every finite Lr(H).
The quantitative residual estimate assumes the additional inequality ⟨A(x)−A(y),x−y⟩≥μ‖x−y‖V^p; ordinary monotonicity does not supply this hypothesis.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC and V compactly embedded in H in a Banach evolution triple. Piecewise-constant states bounded in Lp(V), with backward difference quotients bounded in Lq(V*) for 1<p<∞ and 1<q≤∞ and vanishing maximum time step, are relatively compact in Lp(H). Uniform nodal H bounds give convergence of the same subsequence in every finite Lr(H).
Assume AC. For a Banach evolution triple and 1<p<∞, u∈Lp(V) with u'∈Lp'(V*) has a unique C([0,T];H) representative satisfying ‖u(t)‖H²−‖u(s)‖H²=2∫s^t⟨u',u⟩ for every 0≤s≤t≤T.

Under Countable Choice, fixed-degree zero-boundary Lagrange spaces on the stated globally quasi-uniform shape-regular Lipschitz simplicial meshes, or interval meshes, have uniformly Lr-bounded mass-system projections for 1≤r≤∞, uniformly gradient-stable projections for 1<p<∞, and strong W1p approximation. With AC and the strict PE12 exponent threshold these satisfy the abstract FEM projector clauses.

Under AC, the admissible monotone flux and stable conforming FEM hypotheses, cell-average forcing and projected initial data admit backward Euler solutions. Every such solution has mesh- and time-step-independent nodal H, jump-square, Lp(V), and Lp'(V*) discrete-derivative bounds with the stated data dependencies.
For the stated monotone Carathéodory p-growth flux, weak convergences ξn→ξ in Lp and a(x,ξn)→q in Lp', together with limsup ∫a(x,ξn)·ξn≤∫q·ξ, imply q=a(x,ξ) almost everywhere.

Assume AC. A bounded sequence in Lp(0,T;W0^{1,p}(Ω)) whose images converge strongly in Lp(0,T;H) has a weakly convergent Bochner-Sobolev subsequence; its limit has that H image and its gradients converge weakly in space-time Lp.
Assume AC. For bounded open Ω⊆R^d, d≥1, and 1<p<∞ with p>max(1,2d/(d+2)), W0^{1,p}(Ω) is continuously, compactly and densely embedded in L2(Ω), without boundary regularity.

For the stated fixed-degree globally quasi-uniform nodal spaces, the scaled mass matrix has a uniformly positive bounded spectrum, exponentially decaying inverse entries in nodal graph distance, uniformly summable absolute inverse rows and columns, and the stated local and global coefficient norm equivalences.

Under Countable Choice, Banach-valued Lp functions for finite p have continuous time translations and convergent smooth time mollifications on compact interior intervals; interval averages converge in Lp for partitions with vanishing maximum cell length.

concerns.concern: F2 says, “Bochner time mollification converges in Lp(V) and commutes with the distributional derivative on interior subintervals,” citing lem-pe12-bochner-lp-mollification. That supplier states and proves translation continuity, mollification convergence and interval-average convergence, but does not establish derivative commutation or smooth V-valued differentiation. Step 1.1 uses these additional properties to identify the derivative of the mollification with the mollified u'. The standard scalar-test/Fubini calculation and differentiation of the smooth kernel close this small gap.

seams_checked.note: Checked real evolution pairings, Brouwer step existence, Bochner averages, componentwise weak-gradient extraction and finite-dimensional discrete compactness. The MINI compactness lemma applies PE12 to E→E→E with p=2 and q=4/3, rather than assuming full-test derivative control for weakly solenoidal velocities. No reverse logical dependency was found.

The strict Sobolev exponent, AC, conforming reconstruction, weak-gradient and Minty limsup hypotheses are retained. The computed-state compactness proof explicitly reconstructs the finite-projection argument instead of applying a conforming-state theorem directly to cellwise constants. The conditional identification lemma keeps its assumptions explicit. No reverse logical dependency was found.

This is a contextual page prerequisite. The FAS carriers do not import a PE12 theorem; the semilinear reaction-diffusion example explicitly checks its finite-dimensional monotonicity and convergence hypotheses locally. No unsupported compactness, projector-stability or continuum-limit claim is imported, and no reverse dependency was found.

The conforming interval limit theorem invokes discrete Aubin–Lions with V=H1(0,L), H=L2(0,L), p=q=2, AC and vanishing time steps. Its proof supplies the discrete V* derivative estimate using its own uniformly H1-stable exact-L2 projector. It does not import PE12's zero-boundary projector theorem into the Neumann setting. No reverse dependency was found.
